title: Bundle full runtime and base model in a per-user Windows installer
context: Target PCs may have no Python, Node, or GPU, and users may not be able to install software or get admin rights. The app needed to run after a single installer on a machine with only Chrome or Edge.
decision: Build MeetingTranscriber-Setup-<version>.exe with Inno Setup. It installs per user (no admin) to a fixed folder and bundles a portable node.exe, an embeddable CPython 3.12 with CPU-only faster-whisper, the prebuilt web app, and the Whisper base model as a plain folder that loads offline. Launchers are path-relative. Upgrade and uninstall stop only the bundled runtime's processes and keep recordings and downloaded models. The build smoke-tests the bundle with a minimal PATH and HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1. Server and worker changes support this: WHISPER_MODELS_DIR loads <dir>/<name>/model.bin offline, model names must be plain size names, and TRANSCRIBER_PORT lets the staged server run beside a server on 5000.
consequences: The installer is large because it ships Node, CPython, and the base model.
Transcription runs on the CPU. The CUDA libraries are not bundled; the worker tries CUDA and falls back to CPU before reporting ready.
The installer is unsigned, so SmartScreen warns users on first run.
Other Whisper models still download on first use into the bundled models folder.
Upgrade and uninstall replace runtime\ and app\ wholesale, which is why the install folder is fixed.
Model names from requests are restricted to plain size names. Paths and Hugging Face repo ids are rejected with 400 in server.js and ValueError in the worker.
alternatives_rejected: Installer folder-selection page: omitted, because upgrades and uninstall replace runtime\ and app\ wholesale and the fixed folder keeps them predictable.
